issues.description: Race condition on is_registered flag — concurrent first-time LoRA requests can omit weights/config
issues.detail: In `_create_trtllm_generate_request`, the code checks `if not lora_config.is_registered` and then sets `lora_config.is_registered = True` only after populating weights/config inputs. The `TritonLoraConfig` dataclass is shared per-model in `model_metadata`, and FastAPI handles requests concurrently. Two simultaneous first requests for the same LoRA can both read `is_registered == False` and proceed, but the assignment happens at the bottom and there is no lock. Worse, since `is_registered` is mutated on the shared config object, a second request that arrives after the first sets the flag but before the backend actually caches the LoRA in TRT-LLM may send only `lora_task_id` with no weights — TRT-LLM will fail to find the task and the request errors. Use a per-LoRA lock and only set `is_registered` after the backend confirms registration (or always send weights and let TRT-LLM dedupe by task_id).

issues.description: `_get_lora_config` return type annotation lies — function returns None but annotated as TritonLoraConfig
issues.detail: The signature is `def _get_lora_config(self, model_name: str, lora_name: Optional[str]) -> TritonLoraConfig:` but the body returns `None` when `lora_name is None or model_metadata.lora_configs is None`. This is misleading and breaks downstream type assumptions. The annotation should be `Optional[TritonLoraConfig]`. Also, `self.model_metadata.get(model_name)` can return `None`, after which `model_metadata.lora_configs` will raise AttributeError instead of producing a clean ClientError.

issues.description: Local variable `lora_config_path` shadowed inside loop — overwrites outer multi_lora.json path
issues.detail: In `_parse_lora_configs`, `lora_config_path = os.path.join(version_path, 'multi_lora.json')` is set before the loop. Inside the loop iterating over `lora_config.items()`, a new local variable also named `lora_config_path = os.path.join(lora_path, 'model.lora_config.npy')` is created, shadowing the outer one. If multiple repo paths are configured (`repo_paths` list), subsequent iterations of the outer `for repo_path in repo_paths` loop will still reference the old multi_lora.json path correctly on first re-read because it's recomputed each iteration — but it's a confusing bug-magnet. More importantly, the variable name collision masks the original `lora_config` JSON dict name later. Rename the inner to `lora_config_npy_path` and `lora_weights_npy_path`.

issues.description: Path traversal / arbitrary file read via untrusted multi_lora.json paths
issues.detail: `multi_lora.json` entries are interpreted as filesystem paths and `np.load` is called on `os.path.join(lora_path, 'model.lora_*.npy')`. If `lora_path` is absolute or contains `..`, the loader will read arbitrary files outside the model repository. While the operator authors multi_lora.json, the README example uses relative paths but the code accepts absolute paths silently. Validate that resolved `lora_path` stays inside the model version directory (or document the trust model explicitly). Also, `np.load` defaults to `allow_pickle=False` for `.npy` (good), but accepting arbitrary paths still enables information disclosure of any file readable by the server process.

issues.description: task_id allocation is not stable across server restarts and can collide between models
issues.detail: `lora_task_id` starts at 1 and increments per-LoRA across all repo paths in a single call. Different models served concurrently will each get task_ids 1..N independently; if TRT-LLM treats `lora_task_id` as globally scoped per-engine, two different LoRAs from different models can have the same task_id and collide in the engine cache. Also, task_id 0 is skipped (start at 1), which may be deliberate but is undocumented. Make task allocation explicit (per-engine, monotonic, documented) and add a comment about the namespace.

issues.description: LoRA weights loaded synchronously inside the request hot path
issues.detail: On the first request for a given LoRA, `np.load` is called inside `_create_trtllm_generate_request`, which executes on the asyncio event loop. Loading multi-MB `.npy` files from disk blocks the loop and stalls all other in-flight requests. Either (a) preload all LoRA tensors at startup in `_parse_lora_configs` and cache them on the `TritonLoraConfig`, or (b) move the load to a thread executor via `asyncio.to_thread`.

issues.description: Backend selection logic obscures intent and may misroute mixed-backend repos
issues.detail: `backend if self.backend is None else self.backend` is invoked in `_get_model_metadata`. This means if the engine was constructed with a fixed `self.backend`, all models are forced to use that backend's LoRA parser regardless of their actual backend. That contradicts the per-model `backend` detection a few lines above and can lead to a vLLM model being parsed as TRT-LLM (skipping `model.json` enable_lora check) or vice versa. The conditional should always use the per-model `backend`, or the precedence should be documented.

issues.description: `_parse_lora_configs` return type annotation is wrong
issues.detail: Signature claims `-> None | List[tuple[str, str]]`, but the function returns `List[TritonLoraConfig]` (or `None`). The type lie was carried over from the rename. Update to `Optional[List[TritonLoraConfig]]`.

issues.description: Exception swallowing returns None and loses context for TRT-LLM case
issues.detail: When `multi_lora.json` parsing fails for the TRT-LLM backend, the bare `except Exception` catches everything (including programmer errors and ServerError-like signals), prints traceback to stdout, and returns `None`. This makes operator misconfiguration silently degrade to 'no LoRAs available' instead of surfacing a clear error. ServerError is rethrown explicitly (good), but other exceptions like JSON parse failure or KeyError become invisible. Prefer narrow `except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError)` and log via logger, not `print`.

issues.description: Debug `print(f"backend: {backend}")` left inside per-LoRA loop
issues.detail: Line 681 contains `print(f"backend: {backend}")` inside the inner loop. This is clearly leftover debug output that will spam stdout once per LoRA per model on every metadata refresh. Remove or convert to debug-level logging.

issues.description: `print(traceback.format_exc())` added to FastAPI exception handlers — should use logger
issues.detail: chat.py, completions.py, embeddings.py all add `print(traceback.format_exc())` in `except ServerError` and `except Exception` blocks. (1) The 5xx path now writes the traceback to stdout uncontrollably, which is fine in dev but bypasses structured logging in production. (2) The 4xx ClientError path doesn't trace, but a programmer error masquerading as ClientError will silently hide. Use the framework logger (`logger.exception(...)`) and respect log-level configuration.

issues.description: Skipped tests dropped `@unittest.skipUnless(is_vllm_installed())` without equivalent skip for missing trtllm
issues.detail: Previously all three tests had `@unittest.skipUnless(is_vllm_installed(), 'vLLM not installed')`. After the change, `_backend` is computed at class-definition time as `'vllm' if is_vllm_installed() else 'tensorrtllm'`. If neither backend is installed (or trtllm path requires a built engine that's not present), tests will execute and fail rather than skip. Also, `_model_name` is captured at class definition; if `is_vllm_installed()` is non-deterministic across imports or environments, this conflates testing both backends. Consider parametrizing the test class by backend and skipping when neither prerequisite is available.

issues.description: test_parse_lora_configs invokes both backends but only the vllm path validates expected behavior
issues.detail: The test now calls `parse_lora_configs(model_repository, model_name, 1, 'vllm')` immediately followed by `parse_lora_configs(model_repository, model_name, 1, 'tensorrtllm')` and only asserts on ValueError. The TRT-LLM call against a vLLM-shaped test fixture is essentially a smoke call that may return None without exercising the new code path (missing multi_lora.json → `continue`). The test does not verify that TRT-LLM LoRA discovery correctly produces `TritonLoraConfig` with `path`, `task_id`, and validates missing `.npy` files. Add a positive-path test.

issues.description: Loading `.npy` data into `inputs["lora_weights"]` without shape/dtype validation
issues.detail: `np.load` results are passed directly to Triton inputs without checking the array shape, dtype, or whether they match the engine's `max_lora_rank` / `lora_target_modules`. A malformed `.npy` (e.g., wrong rank, wrong dtype) will reach the backend and produce an obscure CUDA/engine error rather than a useful client-facing message. Validate at parse time or wrap in a clear ServerError.

issues.description: `is_registered: Optional[bool] = False` — Optional bool with default False is semantically just bool
issues.detail: `Optional[bool] = False` allows `None`, which is never used. Use `bool = False`. Minor type hygiene.

issues.description: Cloud model_path branch still returns `None` on `model.json` parse failure for TRT-LLM, but model.json is not used for TRT-LLM
issues.detail: The earlier early-return `return None` branches (e.g., when the cloud directory can't be located) were originally tied to vLLM `model.json` semantics. For TRT-LLM, returning None silently disables LoRA discovery without explanation. Consider distinguishing 'no LoRA configured for this backend' from 'model directory malformed' so operators can debug.

issues.description: README example uses relative paths but resolution semantics not documented
issues.detail: The README example shows `"doll": "inflight_batcher_llm/tensorrt_llm_bls/1/luotuo-lora-7b-0.1-weights"` — relative to what cwd? The server's working directory? Document that paths in `multi_lora.json` are resolved as-is (`os.path.join(lora_path, ...)`) and must be either absolute or relative to the server cwd to avoid operator confusion.

issues.description: test fixture copytree `tests/tensorrtllm_models` referenced but not added to the diff
issues.detail: `_create_trtllm_model_repository_with_lora` and `_without_lora` call `shutil.copytree('tests/tensorrtllm_models', 'models')`. The diff does not show this fixture being added — confirm it exists in-repo or is generated by the L0 test harness. If absent, tests will fail in any CI not run through the L0 wrapper.

issues.description: FIXME WAR in test.sh patches `dims: [ -1, 3 ]` to `[ -1, 4 ]` via sed
issues.detail: qa/L0_openai/test.sh contains a sed-based workaround for a TRT-LLM config issue with a FIXME note. This is acceptable as a tactical fix, but file an issue link in the comment so the WAR can be removed when upstream stabilizes.

issues.description: `tensorrtllm_mistral_models/` added to .gitignore without explanation
issues.detail: New ignore entry but no docs/test referencing it. Either remove or add a comment indicating which test generates this directory.

dissents.topic: How to handle TRT-LLM LoRA registration state (is_registered flag)

positions.position: Mutating shared `is_registered` on the metadata-level `TritonLoraConfig` is fundamentally unsafe under asyncio + threaded uvicorn. Move state into a per-engine registry keyed by task_id with an asyncio.Lock and serialize first-load.

Always send `lora_weights` and `lora_config` along with `lora_task_id` on every request; TRT-LLM dedupes by task_id and the cost is one extra payload. This trades a small amount of bandwidth for eliminating the entire race condition class and removes mutable state.

dissents.topic: Whether multi_lora.json paths should be sandboxed

positions.position: Operator-authored config can still be a vector — validate paths stay within the model repository, reject absolute paths and `..`, and document the trust model.

multi_lora.json is authored by the same operator who configures the model repo and CLI args; treating it as trusted is consistent with the rest of the system. Validation adds friction without raising the security bar meaningfully.

dissents.topic: Where to load LoRA weights (startup vs first-request)

positions.position: Load on first request keeps startup fast and avoids loading LoRAs that may never be used — acceptable if first-request latency for that LoRA is documented.
Synchronous `np.load` on the asyncio path blocks the loop and tanks tail latency for every other in-flight request. Preload at startup or dispatch the load to a thread executor.

dissents.topic: Test class design after dropping vLLM skip decorators

positions.position: Compute backend at class-def time and dispatch via if/elif — simple and matches the existing test style.
Parametrize the test class by backend with skipUnless gates per backend so both backends can be exercised in environments that have both, and neither environment misreports failures as skips.

review.summary: This PR extends LoRA support to the TensorRT-LLM backend in the OpenAI-compatible frontend. The core design — generalize `lora_names` to `lora_configs: List[TritonLoraConfig]` and add per-backend parsing — is reasonable, but several issues should block merge. The most serious is a race condition on the shared `is_registered` flag: under concurrent first-time requests for the same LoRA, two requests can both see `is_registered=False`, but only one sends the weights, and the other may reach TRT-LLM before the backend has actually cached the task — produce request errors. The path traversal exposure via untrusted `multi_lora.json` entries and the synchronous `np.load` blocking the asyncio event loop are also significant. Type annotations on `_get_lora_config` and `_parse_lora_configs` are wrong, leftover `print` statements indicate the diff was not cleaned up, and test coverage for the positive TRT-LLM parse path is missing. The `print(traceback.format_exc())` additions across routers should use the logger. Recommend addressing the race condition, the path safety, the event-loop blocking, and the type/log hygiene before merging; the LoRA cache strategy is also worth a brief design discussion (preload vs. always-send-weights).
